sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是99%隐形节目。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: In the late 1960s, an Italian industrialist and a Scottish scientist started a club to address what they considered to be humankind's greatest probleMs.
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代末，一位意大利实业家和一位苏格兰科学家发起了一个俱乐部，旨在应对他们认为的全人类最大的问题。

sentences.en: Things like pollution, resource scarcity, and overpopulation.
sentences.zh: 比如污染、资源匮乏和人口过剩。

sentences.en: And because this group met in Rome, Italy, it came to be known as the Club of Rome.
sentences.zh: 因为这个小组在意大利罗马开会，所以它被称为罗马俱乐部。

sentences.en: Producer Katie Mingle.
sentences.zh: 制作人凯蒂·明格尔。

sentences.en: Over the next couple of years, the Club of Rome would grow to include politicians, scientists, economists, and business leaders from around the world.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几年里，罗马俱乐部不断发展壮大，吸纳了来自世界各地的政治家、科学家、经济学家和商界领袖。

sentences.en: It was a pretty elite group.
sentences.zh: 这是一个相当精英的组织。

sentences.en: I've always pictured a lot of leather, furniture, and cigar smoking.
sentences.zh: 我脑海中总是浮现出大量的真皮家具和雪茄烟雾的画面。

sentences.en: I don't know how much cigar smoking there was.
sentences.zh: 我不知道当时抽雪茄的现象有多少。

sentences.en: I mean, it was certainly clubby.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它确实很有俱乐部色彩。

sentences.en: That's Patrick McRae.
sentences.zh: 那是帕特里克·麦克雷。

sentences.en: He's a professor of history at the University of California, Santa Barbara.
sentences.zh: 他是加州大学圣巴巴拉分校的历史学教授。

sentences.en: I think there certainly was a tendency to imagine them as sort of this cigar smoking cabal, you know, sort of pulling the strings behind the scenes.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们确实倾向于把他们想象成那种抽雪茄的秘密集团，你知道的，就像在幕后操纵一切一样。

sentences.en: But I think there was a genuine interest on their part to address these problems of the world.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们内心确实有一种真诚的愿望去解决这些世界性的问题。

sentences.en: The people who were a part of the Club of Rome basically wanted to figure out if and when the world was going to hit maximum capacity and run out of resources.
sentences.zh: 罗马俱乐部的成员基本上是想弄清楚世界是否以及何时会达到最大承载能力并耗尽资源。

sentences.en: And toward this end, they had a tool, a relatively new tool at the time, the computer.
sentences.zh: 为了达到这个目的，他们使用了一个工具，一个当时相对较新的工具：计算机。

sentences.en: And so they plugged a bunch of data into their huge 1970s computers.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们把一堆数据输入到他们20世纪70年代的巨型计算机中。

sentences.en: And then looked at the results and switched up the variables and ran the tests again.
sentences.zh: 然后查看结果，改变变量，再次进行测试。

sentences.en: No matter how they played with the variables, which were resource use, pollution, industrialization, population growth, things like that.
sentences.zh: 无论他们如何调整这些变量——资源使用、污染、工业化、人口增长等等。

sentences.en: All of the models that they came up with, all of them sort of led to the same conclusion.
sentences.zh: 他们得出的所有模型，无一例外都导向了同一个结论。

sentences.en: Sometime in the 21st century, there would be this massive collapse of global society.
sentences.zh: 在21世纪的某个时候，全球社会将会发生巨大的崩溃。

sentences.en: In 1972, the Club of Rome published a book outlining their findings called The Limits to Growth.
sentences.zh: 1972年，罗马俱乐部出版了一本书，概述了他们的研究结果，名为《增长的极限》。

sentences.en: And it got a lot of media attention.
sentences.zh: 这引起了媒体的大量关注。

sentences.en: They found the way things are going now, the planet can support us for less than 100 years.
sentences.zh: 他们发现按照目前的状况发展下去，地球支撑我们的时间不到100年。

sentences.en: It may be nearer 50.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能接近50年。

sentences.en: The book became a surprise bestseller and was translated into more than two dozen languages.
sentences.zh: 这本书出人意料地成为畅销书，被翻译成了二十多种语言。

sentences.en: And yeah, there were critics who disagreed with the findings.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有批评者不同意这些研究结果。

sentences.en: But overall, The Limits to Growth was incredibly influential.
sentences.zh: 但总体而言，《增长的极限》具有难以置信的影响力。

sentences.en: You know, there was a famous cover of Newsweek around 1973 that shows Uncle Sam on the cover looking into a cornucopia.
sentences.zh: 你知道，1973年前后《新闻周刊》有一期著名的封面，上面画着山姆大叔正看着一个聚宝盆。

sentences.en: And there's nothing in it.
sentences.zh: 而里面空无一物。

sentences.en: And the headline on the cover of Newsweek says,
sentences.zh: 《新闻周刊》封面上的标题写着：

sentences.en: Running Out of Everything.
sentences.zh: 《万物告罄》。

sentences.en: You could see the idea of limits all over popular culture.
sentences.zh: 你可以在流行文化的各个角落看到关于极限的想法。

sentences.en: New York City in the year 2022.
sentences.zh: 2022年的纽约市。

sentences.en: Nothing runs anymore.
sentences.zh: 什么都不再运转了。

sentences.en: Nothing works.
sentences.zh: 什么都不起作用了。

sentences.en: The famous or infamous movie with Charlton Heston, Soylent Green.
sentences.zh: 查尔斯·赫斯顿主演的那部著名或声名狼藉的电影《超世纪谍杀案》。

sentences.en: I mean, the whole premise of the movie is based on a scenario where there's overpopulation
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这部电影的整个前提都是基于这样一个场景：人口过剩

sentences.en: and the earth has, you know, has exceeded its carrying capacity.
sentences.zh: 而且地球已经，你知道的，超过了它的承载能力。

sentences.en: But the people are the same.
sentences.zh: 但人们还是那些人。

sentences.en: And the people will do anything to get what they need.
sentences.zh: 人们会不惜一切代价得到他们需要的东西。

sentences.en: This is the police.
sentences.zh: 这里是警察。

sentences.en: What they need most is Soylent Green.
sentences.zh: 他们最需要的是人造滋养饼。

sentences.en: But I think there was this really fierce debate that the Limits to Growth report stimulated
sentences.zh: 但我觉得《增长的极限》报告引发了一场非常激烈的辩论

sentences.en: about whether there was this need to curtail economic growth and to regulate populations
sentences.zh: 关于是否有必要遏制经济增长、控制人口

sentences.en: and perhaps even curtail individual freedoMs.
sentences.zh: 甚至可能遏制个人自由。

sentences.en: And out of this chorus of debate and alarm emerges a physicist and engineer named Gerard O'Neill.
sentences.zh: 在这片辩论和警示的合唱中，一位名叫杰拉德·奥尼尔的物理学家兼工程师崭露头角。

sentences.en: He was mostly known as Jerry.
sentences.zh: 他通常被称为杰瑞。

sentences.en: And Jerry O'Neill says,
sentences.zh: 杰瑞·奥尼尔说：

sentences.en: Yeah, we may live on a limited planet, but we live in a limitless universe.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们可能生活在一个有限的星球上，但我们生活在一个无限的宇宙中。

sentences.en: And the answer to a lot of our problems here on earth may actually be out in space,
sentences.zh: 解决我们在地球上面临的许多问题的答案，实际上可能在太空中

sentences.en: in what O'Neill called the high frontier.
sentences.zh: 在奥尼尔所称的高边疆中。

sentences.en: Here's Jerry O'Neill in an archival recording from the 70s.
sentences.zh: 这里是70年代杰瑞·奥尼尔的档案录音。

sentences.en: Opening the high frontier means making possible and ensuring the survival of the human race.
sentences.zh: 开辟高边疆意味着使人类种族的生存成为可能并得到保障。

sentences.en: Jerry O'Neill wanted to build settlements in space.
sentences.zh: 杰瑞·奥尼尔想要在太空中建立定居点。

sentences.en: If you truly love this planet, the best thing you can do for it is to move as much industry
sentences.zh: 如果你真心热爱这个星球，你能为它做的最好的事情，就是将尽可能多的工业

sentences.en: and as many people as possible from its surface out into space.
sentences.zh: 以及尽可能多的人口从地表转移到太空中去。

sentences.en: O'Neill was motivated and really saw his ideas as a form of environmentalism.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔受到这种动机的驱使，并真正将自己的想法视为一种环保主义形式。

sentences.en: Jerry O'Neill wasn't the first person to imagine human habitats in space.
sentences.zh: 杰瑞·奥尼尔并不是第一个想象人类太空栖息地的人。

sentences.en: But unlike others who had come before him, O'Neill was the first to crunch all the numbers
sentences.zh: 但与之前其他人不同的是，奥尼尔是第一个进行所有数据测算

sentences.en: and come up with technologically feasible designs.
sentences.zh: 并提出技术上可行设计的人。

sentences.en: Over the course of his work, he would turn skeptics into true believers, find support from NASA,
sentences.zh: 在其工作过程中，他将怀疑论者变成了忠实的信徒，获得了美国宇航局的支持

sentences.en: and start a social movement toward the goal of building human colonies in space.
sentences.zh: 并发起了一场旨在建立人类太空殖民地的社会运动。

sentences.en: Before he started thinking about space colonies, Jerry O'Neill was a professor in Princeton's
sentences.zh: 在开始思考太空殖民地之前，杰瑞·奥尼尔是普林斯顿大学

sentences.en: physics department.
sentences.zh: 物理系的一名教授。

sentences.en: But he wasn't content analyzing data.
sentences.zh: 但他并不满足于分析数据。

sentences.en: He liked building things.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢亲手建造东西。

sentences.en: O'Neill's contribution to physics was re-engineering the way in which particle accelerators were designed
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔对物理学的贡献在于重新设计了粒子加速器的设计和制造方式

sentences.en: and built.
sentences.zh: 并将其建造出来。

sentences.en: And he was really, really successful at this.
sentences.zh: 他在这一领域取得了巨大成功。

sentences.en: He was very famous already as a physicist long before he got interested in space colonies.
sentences.zh: 早在对太空殖民产生兴趣之前，他作为一名物理学家就已经非常著名了。

sentences.en: So he was very much respected among his equals and a person of great character.
sentences.zh: 因此，他在同仁中备受尊敬，是一个极具品格的人。

sentences.en: I always got along very well with him.
sentences.zh: 我和他一直相处得很好。

sentences.en: That's Freeman Dyson.
sentences.zh: 那是弗里曼·戴森。

sentences.en: Yes, I'm Freeman Dyson.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是弗里曼·戴森。

sentences.en: I'm a retired professor at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
sentences.zh: 我是普林斯顿高等研究院的退休教授。

sentences.en: My subject was mathematics and physics.
sentences.zh: 我的专业是数学和物理。

sentences.en: I was just a pencil pusher, scribbling equations.
sentences.zh: 我只是个推敲公式、涂涂画画的书呆子。

sentences.en: Dyson is being modeSt.
sentences.zh: 戴森太谦虚了。

sentences.en: He was and is a polymath and a veritable genius.
sentences.zh: 他过去是、现在也是一位博学者和真正的天才。

sentences.en: He's made huge contributions in quantum mechanics, but also in nuclear energy, biology, and astrophysics.
sentences.zh: 他在量子力学、核能、生物学和天体物理学领域都做出了巨大贡献。

sentences.en: And he's got pop culture cred, too.
sentences.zh: 他也有流行文化影响力。

sentences.en: There's a video game character named after him.
sentences.zh: 有一个电子游戏角色就是以他的名字命名的。

sentences.en: There's even a Star Trek episode about one of his concepts.
sentences.zh: 甚至还有一集《星际迷航》探讨了他的一个概念。

sentences.en: Dyson was also a friend and colleague to Jerry O'Neill.
sentences.zh: 戴森也是杰瑞·奥尼尔的朋友和同事。

sentences.en: O'Neill died in 1992.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔于1992年逝世。

sentences.en: He had many students who were always following him around.
sentences.zh: 他有许多总是跟在他身边的学生。

sentences.en: He actually got his students doing real projects.
sentences.zh: 他实际上让他的学生们去做真正的项目。

sentences.en: It wasn't just talk.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是空谈。

sentences.en: In 1969, the same year the first astronauts walked on the moon,
sentences.zh: 1969年，也就是第一批宇航员登上月球的同一年，

sentences.en: O'Neill posed a question to his introductory physics students at Princeton.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔向他在普林斯顿大学的物理学入门班学生提出了一个问题。

sentences.en: What makes more sense, building human settlements on the surface of another planet
sentences.zh: 在另一个星球表面建立人类定居点，

sentences.en: or building free-floating settlements in outer space?
sentences.zh: 还是在外太空建立自由漂浮的定居点，哪个更有意义？

sentences.en: Through months of research and calculations, O'Neill and his students came to the conclusion
sentences.zh: 经过几个月的调研和计算，奥尼尔和他的学生们得出结论

sentences.en: that building free-floating habitats was the way to go.
sentences.zh: 建造自由漂浮的栖息地才是正确的方向。

sentences.en: First of all, you don't have to overcome gravity every time you go on and off a free-floating space settlement.
sentences.zh: 首先，每次进出自由漂浮的太空定居点时，你都不需要克服重力。

sentences.en: But even more importantly, in space, you have access to the sun's energy 100% of the time.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，在太空中，你可以百分之百的时间利用太阳能。

sentences.en: So no other sources of fuel would be needed.
sentences.zh: 因此不需要任何其他燃料来源。

sentences.en: But when the semester ended, O'Neill didn't stop thinking about space colonization.
sentences.zh: 但当学期结束时，奥尼尔并没有停止对太空殖民的思考。

sentences.en: In fact, he'd only just begun.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他才刚刚开始。

sentences.en: It wasn't just dreams of some rather remote future.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是对某个相当遥远未来的梦想。

sentences.en: It was something O'Neill really thought he could do.
sentences.zh: 这是奥尼尔真正认为自己能够做到的事情。

sentences.en: O'Neill decided he would build his settlements at a place in our solar system
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔决定将他的定居点建在我们太阳系中

sentences.en: 250,000 miles from the Earth called Lagrange or Lagrange Point 5.
sentences.zh: 距离地球25万英里、被称为拉格朗日点或拉格朗日5号点的地方。

sentences.en: Lagrange points are places in space where objects stay put.
sentences.zh: 拉格朗日点是太空中物体可以保持静止的位置。

sentences.en: They don't move around on orbits.
sentences.zh: 它们不会在轨道上到处移动。

sentences.en: And so these are the most convenient places if you want to have a fixed habitat.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果你想拥有一个固定的栖息地，这些就是最方便的地方。

sentences.en: Objects stay put because at Lagrange Point 5, or L5,
sentences.zh: 物体之所以能保持静止，是因为在拉格朗日5号点，即L5点，

sentences.en: the gravity of the sun and Earth are at a special equilibrium.
sentences.zh: 太阳和地球的引力处于一种特殊的平衡状态。

sentences.en: L5 was his favorite Lagrange Point,
sentences.zh: L5是他最喜欢的拉格朗日点，

sentences.en: a place which is the same distance from the moon and the Earth.
sentences.zh: 一个距离月球和地球距离相等的地方。

sentences.en: All of O'Neill's designs for habitats were variations on cylinders, spheres, or ring shapes.
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔所有的栖息地设计都是圆柱体、球体或环形的变体。

sentences.en: And his designs have been copied all over science fiction.
sentences.zh: 他的设计被科幻小说界广泛模仿。

sentences.en: You can see O'Neill-esque designs in the movies Elysium and Interstellar, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，你可以在电影《极乐空间》和《星际穿越》中看到带有奥尼尔风格的设计。

sentences.en: The design that I find the easiest to picture
sentences.zh: 我发现最容易想象的设计

sentences.en: basically looks like a giant bicycle wheel floating in space.
sentences.zh: 基本上看起来就像一个漂浮在太空中的巨大自行车轮。

sentences.en: The people would live inside the tire part of the wheel,
sentences.zh: 人们会住在车轮的轮胎部分里面，

sentences.en: which itself would be enormous.
sentences.zh: 而这个部分本身将是极其巨大的。

sentences.en: There would be huge windows that let in sunlight
sentences.zh: 会有巨大的窗户引入阳光，

sentences.en: and allowed amazing views of outer space.
sentences.zh: 并能欣赏到太空中令人惊叹的景色。

sentences.en: The artist's renderings of O'Neill's settlements
sentences.zh: 艺术家对奥尼尔定居点的效果图

sentences.en: make them look really earth-like and appealing,
sentences.zh: 让他们看起来非常像地球且极具吸引力，

sentences.en: with water and trees and terraced housing.
sentences.zh: 有水、树木和阶梯式住宅。

sentences.en: He imagined that, you know, it would be like an Italian hill town.
sentences.zh: 他想象着，你知道的，这会像一个意大利的山城。

sentences.en: We knew that the first ones wouldn't look like anything like that.
sentences.zh: 我们知道最初的那些看起来绝对不会是那个样子。

sentences.en: That's Tasha O'Neill.
sentences.zh: 那是塔莎·奥尼尔。

sentences.en: In 1969, Tasha had just moved to the U.S.
sentences.zh: 1969年，塔莎刚从德国搬到美国做互惠生，

sentences.en: from Germany to work as an au pair
sentences.zh: 当时她决定去参加一个基督教青年会的联谊活动。

sentences.en: when she decided to attend a mixer at the YMCA.
sentences.zh: 杰瑞·奥尼尔頂着一头蓬松的拖把头走了进来，

sentences.en: In walked Jerry O'Neill with his mop-top haircut,
sentences.zh: 与其说他像个物理学家，倒不如说他更像60年代摇滚乐队的成员。

sentences.en: looking more like a member of a 60s rock band than a physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 我看着他心想，

sentences.en: I looked at him and I thought,
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是我在这里看到的第一个有趣的人。

sentences.en: hmm, that's the first interesting guy that I see around here.
sentences.zh: 我不会说这是一见钟情，

sentences.en: I wouldn't say it was love at first sight,
sentences.zh: 但这绝对是一见倾心，

sentences.en: but it was definitely interest at first sight,
sentences.zh: 这份倾心很快就发展成了爱情。

sentences.en: which grew into love very quickly.
sentences.zh: 当他和塔莎相遇时，

sentences.en: When he and Tasha met,
sentences.zh: 奥尼尔刚开始认真思考太空殖民的问题，

sentences.en: O'Neill had just started seriously thinking about space colonies,
sentences.zh: 他渴望与她分享自己的想法。

sentences.en: and he was eager to share his ideas with her.
sentences.zh: 我觉得很讽刺的是，我竟然会遇到并嫁给一位物理学家。

sentences.en: I thought it was really ironic that I would meet and marry a physiciSt.
sentences.zh: 我的物理知识为零。

sentences.en: My physics was non-existent.
sentences.zh: 我这门课不及格。

sentences.en: I flunked it.
sentences.zh: 但他非常擅长向外行人解释事情。

sentences.en: But he was so good at explaining things to lay people.
sentences.zh: 塔莎也变得擅长解释他的想法。

sentences.en: And Tasha also got good at explaining his ideas.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，她向我解释说，

sentences.en: She explained to me, for example,
sentences.zh: 人们居住的那个车轮

sentences.en: that the wheel in which people would live
sentences.zh: 会沿着一个轴非常缓慢地旋转，

sentences.en: would rotate very slowly on an axis,
sentences.zh: 而这种旋转产生的离心力

sentences.en: and the centrifugal force of that rotation
sentences.zh: 会为里面的人创造一种类似重力的感觉

sentences.en: would create a gravity-like sensation for the people inside
sentences.zh: （此处为补充结束位，由于原封顶149已对应完毕）

sentences.en: to keep them from floating around.
sentences.zh: 为了防止它们漂浮乱飞。

sentences.en: The rotating would have been very slow,
sentences.zh: 旋转的速度本来会非常慢，

sentences.en: and you would not have noticed it.
sentences.zh: 而且你根本不会注意到。

sentences.en: But the closer you were to the axis,
sentences.zh: 但你离轴心，

sentences.en: or the center of the wheel,
sentences.zh: 也就是轮子的中心越近，

sentences.en: the less gravity you'd experience.

sentences.en: The shuttles ended up making far fewer flights into space than originally predicted.
sentences.zh: 这些航天飞机最终飞往太空的次数远远少于最初的预测。

sentences.en: And in general, NASA became more cautious and less adventurous than a lot of people had hoped.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，美国宇航局变得更加谨慎，不像许多人希望的那样具有冒险精神。

sentences.en: Which is why, in 1977, O'Neill founded the non-profit Space Studies Institute,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在1977年，奥尼尔创立了非营利组织太空研究所，

sentences.en: which raises its own money and does its own research on space colonization.
sentences.zh: 它筹集自己的资金并对太空殖民进行自己的研究。

sentences.en: Gerard O'Neill died in 1992 after a long battle with leukemia.
sentences.zh: 杰勒德·奥尼尔在与白血病长期搏斗后于1992年逝世。

sentences.en: And now, 25 years after his death, some people think that we're on the brink of another space age,
sentences.zh: 现在，在他逝世25年后，一些人认为我们正处于另一个太空时代的边缘，

sentences.en: one that could lead to the realization of some of O'Neill's dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 一个可能导致奥尼尔的一些梦想成为现实的时代。

sentences.en: There are a lot of people working on it.
sentences.zh: 有很多人在为此努力。

sentences.en: He had so many young people working with him.
sentences.zh: 他有那么多年轻人跟他一起工作。

sentences.en: They're now calling themselves Jerry's kids.
sentences.zh: 他们现在自称为杰里的孩子们。

sentences.en: And they're in their 50s.
sentences.zh: 他们现在已经五十多岁了。

sentences.en: But they learned, you know, sitting at his knee.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，他们是在他膝下学习的。

sentences.en: You know, Rick Tomlinson, Peter Diamandis.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，里克·汤姆林森、彼得·戴曼迪斯。

sentences.en: My mission in life since I was a kid was and is to take the rest of you into space.
sentences.zh: 我从小到大的人生使命过去是，现在也是，带你们其余的人进入太空。

sentences.en: It's during our lifetime that we're going to take the people of Earth and transition off permanently.
sentences.zh: 正是在我们这一代人里，我们要带走地球上的人并永久搬迁。

sentences.en: That is Peter Diamandis giving a TED Talk in 2005.
sentences.zh: 那是彼得·戴曼迪斯在2005年的一次TED演讲。

sentences.en: We've thought about the government always as the person taking us there.
sentences.zh: 我们一直认为政府是带我们去那里的人。

sentences.en: But I put forward here, the government is not going to get us there.
sentences.zh: 但我在这里提出，政府不会带我们去那里。

sentences.en: The government is unable to take the risks required to open up this precious frontier.
sentences.zh: 政府无法承担开拓这片珍贵前沿所需的风险。

sentences.en: Like Jerry O'Neill, Diamandis believes that technology can solve humanity's biggest probleMs.
sentences.zh: 就像杰里·奥尼尔一样，戴曼迪斯相信科技可以解决人类最大的问题。

sentences.en: And that we don't have to live in a world of limits.
sentences.zh: 我们不必生活在一个充满限制的世界里。

sentences.en: But unlike O'Neill, Diamandis has another primary motivation.
sentences.zh: 但与奥尼尔不同的是，戴曼迪斯还有另一个主要动力。

sentences.en: Money.
sentences.zh: 金钱。

sentences.en: The universe is full of valuable things to exploit for wealth.
sentences.zh: 宇宙中充满了有价值的东西，可以开采以获取财富。

sentences.en: If you think about space, everything we hold of value on this planet,
sentences.zh: 如果你想想太空，我们在这个星球上认为有价值的一切，

sentences.en: metals and minerals and real estate and energy,
sentences.zh: 金属、矿物、房地产和能源，

sentences.en: is in infinite quantities in space.
sentences.zh: 在太空中都是无限量的。

sentences.en: In fact, the Earth is a crumb in a supermarket filled with resources.
sentences.zh: 事实上，地球只是资源丰富的超级市场里的一块面包屑。

sentences.en: There are other entrepreneurs, like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos,
sentences.zh: 还有其他企业家，比如埃隆·马斯克和杰夫·贝佐斯，

sentences.en: who would also like to make money in space and build human settlements there.
sentences.zh: 他们也想在太空中赚钱并在那里建立人类定居点。

sentences.en: However it happens, both Freeman Dyson and Tasha O'Neill are sure humans will find their way
sentences.zh: 无论如何发生，弗里曼·戴森和塔莎·奥尼尔都确信人类最终会找到自己的路

sentences.en: into settlements in space eventually.
sentences.zh: 进入太空定居点。

sentences.en: Well, I would say it certainly will happen one day.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我会说总有一天这一定会发生。

sentences.en: It's all a question of when.
sentences.zh: 这只是个时间问题。

sentences.en: And I'm counting on it because Jerry wanted his ashes to be scattered in a space colony.
sentences.zh: 我指望这一点，因为杰里希望他的骨灰撒在太空殖民地中。

sentences.en: And I think by now, you know, his grandchildren will,
sentences.zh: 我想到现在，你知道的，他的孙辈会，

sentences.en: or I hope not his great-grandchildren, but somebody will have to do it.
sentences.zh: 或者我希望不是他的曾孙，但总得有人这么做。
